title: X-VLA: Soft-Prompted Transformer as Scalable Cross-Embodiment Vision-Language-Action Model
claim: One simple prompt-conditioned transformer handles heterogeneous data sources, scales in pretraining, adapts widely, and beats all prior models across benchmarks.
layout: Top-left architecture, top-right radar chart, bottom two panels for pretraining and adaptation
description: A composite figure. The top-left panel is a beige X-VLA architecture box. A Soft Prompt Library of color-coded embodiment tokens (Agibot, Agilex, Franka, UR5) feeds learnable prompt tokens. These join a language instruction, camera images, a pretrained VLM, a vision encoder and proprioceptive input. All of them enter a dark stack of soft-prompted self-attention Transformer blocks labelled xN. At top right, a radar chart compares X-VLA-0.9B (orange) against the best of 23 existing models (blue) on about 12 benchmarks, under the caption 'One Model to Beat Them All'. The bottom row has two rounded panels. 'Scalable Cross-embodiment Pretraining' shows a falling training-error curve and a scaling icon. 'Strong Adaptation Capability' shows robot photos, simulator thumbnails, dexterous-task frames and a LoRA tuning schematic. The eye goes first to the architecture and the radar plot. The crop also includes the paper's abstract text above the figure.
caption: X-VLA employs distinctive learnable embeddings, referred to as soft prompt, to effectively address the heterogeneity present in cross-embodiment datasets. This approach, combined with stacking simple self-attention transformer blocks, provides a scalable solution for integrating diverse pretraining datasets and finetuning for a variety of domain-specific applications. Evaluated across 6 simulation benchmark including one autonomous driving bench and 3 real-world robots, X-VLA achieves SOTA performance over most benchmark suites and real-world robotic tasks.
abstract: Successful generalist Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models rely on effective training across diverse robotic platforms with large-scale, cross-embodiment, heterogeneous datasets. To facilitate and leverage the heterogeneity in rich, diverse robotic data sources, we propose a novel Soft Prompt approach with minimally added parameters, by infusing prompt learning concepts into cross-embodiment robot learning and introducing separate sets of learnable embeddings for each distinct data source. These embeddings serve as embodiment-specific prompts, which in unity empower VLA models with effective exploitation of varying cross-embodiment features. Our new X-VLA, a neat flow-matching-based VLA architecture, relies exclusively on soft-prompted standard Transformer encoders, enjoying both scalability and simplicity. Evaluated across 6 simulations as well as 3 real-world robots, our 0.9B instantiation-X-VLA-0.9B simultaneously achieves SOTA performance over a sweep of benchmarks, demonstrating superior results on a wide axes of capabilities, from flexible dexterity to quick adaptation across embodiments, environments, and tasks. Website: https://thu-air-dream.github.io/X-VLA/
